heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

COPY OF THE REGENT OF PROBOLINGGO

PROVINCE OF EAST JAVA

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF PROBOLINGGO REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Probolinggo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Probolinggo Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Probolinggo.
4. Agency is the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of protecting women and children.
5. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development as well as protect women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is established by the Regional Government or community-based.
6. Protection of Women and Children is all activities to protect the rights of women and children and provide a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights without violence and discrimination in accordance with human dignity.
7. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years or a child who is suspected, charged, sentenced to a crime and a child who is a victim of a criminal act.
9. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
10. Discrimination is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of gender, ethnicity, religion, race, and skin color that has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights.
11. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
13. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the self-strengthening of victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
14. Repatriation is an effort to return women and children victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
15. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society.
16. Safe House, hereinafter referred to as Shelter, is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
17. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS OF THE REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Article 4

The Regional Government is obliged to implement the protection of women and children.

heading: Article 5
CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

PLANNING

Article 6

The Regent establishes basic policies for the implementation of protection of women and children in the Region.

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

1. The basic policy as referred to in Article 6 is elaborated in the Regional Action Plan.
2. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) is integrated with the Regional Long-Term Development Plan, Regional Medium-Term Development Plan and Regional Government Work Plan documents.
3. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall at least contain:
a. programs and activities for the protection of women and children, including women and children victims of violence;
b. regional action programs and activities to prevent all forms of violence and discrimination against women and children;
c. programs and activities for improving and enhancing services for the protection of women and children victims of violence; and
d. programs and activities for empowering women and children victims of violence.
4. Provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

The Regional Action Plan must be used as a guideline for the Regional Government in formulating policies related to the implementation of protection of women and children.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

General

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The Regent is obliged to implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in an integrated manner in order to fulfill the rights of women and children in the Region.
2. In carrying out the duties as referred to in paragraph (1), the Agency coordinates with regional apparatus organizations, law enforcement officials and the community.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Forms of Violence

heading: Article 10
Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Physical violence as referred to in Article 10 letter a is caused by acts that result in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 10 letter b is caused by acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

heading: Article 13
Article 14
Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

Exploitation as referred to in Article 10 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and/or
c. any form of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

heading: Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Rights of Victims

heading: Article 16
Article 17
Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. In the event that women and child victims of violence require continuous handling, then women and child victims of violence have the right to stay in a safe house or alternative residence.
2. Continuous handling as referred to in paragraph (1) is handling at the rehabilitation stage, whether carried out by PPT, individuals, non-governmental organizations, or by the community.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Safe houses as referred to in Article 18 paragraph (1) provide temporary safe places and/or shelter for victims of violence until their rights are restored.
2. The operation and/or management of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the relevant Agency.
3. Provisions regarding the operation of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (2) are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Rights of Witnesses and Perpetrators

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential handling, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as wife, mother, child, family member or as a community member.
2. Fulfillment of rights as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Scope

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

Protection of women and child victims of violence includes:
a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. empowerment.

heading: Article 22
Article 23
Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

1. Empowerment as referred to in Article 21 letter c is organized through:
a. job training;
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups; and c. capital assistance.
2. Job training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a includes:
a. skills training;
b. field work practice; and
c. apprenticeship.
3. Productive economic enterprises and joint business groups as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b include:
a. entrepreneurial skills training; and
b. business actor assistance.
4. Capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c includes:
a. facilities and infrastructure assistance; and
b. working/business capital assistance facilities.
5. Empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by PPT.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Special Protection of Children

heading: Article 25
Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Assistance

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Assistance shall be carried out by individuals or institutions that have expertise in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence, perpetrators and witnesses.
2. Provisions regarding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Recovery of Victims, Witnesses, and Perpetrators

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

For the purpose of recovery, women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence may obtain services from:
a. Social institutions (groups or institutions whose scope is on women and children) and or;
b. Social workers (Individuals who have the competence to carry out recovery or rehabilitation) namely:
1\. Nurses
2\. Health workers

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain health examination services by health facilities in accordance with professional standards.
2. In the event that women and children who are victims, witnesses, and perpetrators of violence require treatment, health workers are obliged to provide health recovery and rehabilitation services.
3. The provision of health recovery and rehabilitation services as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. Women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence have the right to obtain counseling services from social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors.
2. Social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors as referred to in paragraph (1) are obliged to provide services to women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence in the form of providing counseling to strengthen, provide a sense of security and rehabilitation.

heading: CHAPTER VI
CHAPTER VII
CHAPTER VIII
Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

In providing protection for women and children, individuals, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, and the business sector shall coordinate with PPT.

heading: Article 34
CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 35

1. The Regent shall conduct guidance and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children, both carried out by PPT and non-governmental organizations.
2. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted in order to realize the objectives of providing protection for women and children in accordance with the mechanisms and service procedures stipulated in laws and regulations.
3. Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the relevant Agency.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. Supervision as referred to in Article 35 shall be conducted on:
a. implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children; and
b. fulfillment of guidelines and minimum service standards in the implementation of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children who are victims of violence.
2. Supervision shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year and the results shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and children for the following year.

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

Provisions regarding guidance and supervision of the provision of protection for women and children shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

REPORTING

Article 38

1. PPT is obligated to report the implementation of protection services for women and children to the Regent through the Agency.
2. Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
3. Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

FUNDING

Article 39

Funds for the implementation of protection for women and children are sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

1. The Regional Government may provide funding assistance to community organizations, social organizations, or non-governmental organizations and universities that carry out protection for women and children.
2. Funding assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided in accordance with regional financial capacity and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XII
Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

PPT organizers or safe houses are prohibited from collecting fees in providing services to women and children who are victims, witnesses and perpetrators of violence.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 43

1. Health Workers who refuse or are unwilling to provide health examination services as referred to in Article 28 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. written warning;
b. suspension of practice license/work permit;
c. restriction of practice for Health Workers in independent practice;
2. Social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors who refuse or are unwilling to provide counseling services as referred to in Article 29 shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. reprimand; or
b. written warning.
3. Provisions regarding the mechanism for imposing sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
CHAPTER XV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XV

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 45

1. Any person who violates the prohibitions as referred to in Article 41 and Article 42 shall be threatened with imprisonment of a maximum of 3 (three) months or a fine of a maximum of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
2. Criminal acts as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are violations.

heading: CHAPTER XVI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 46

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation must be stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this regional regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Probolinggo Regency.

On 1 March 2019
